basis: Ependymal-lined cyst arising within the central nervous system; effects depend on its location and size.
Hereditary sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent pes cavus, clubfoot and kyphoscoliosis each reported in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement.
Teratoma arising in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
B-lineage lymphoblastic neoplasm involving marrow/blood or presenting as lymphoma; both leukemia and lymphoma are included in this concept.
Dysplastic glandular neoplasm originating in the small intestinal epithelium.
Kyphoscoliosis and intellectual disability are defining features, establishing skeletal and neurodevelopmental involvement.
Inflammatory pituitary disease, predominantly autoimmune or immune-mediated; pituitary involvement belongs to the endocrine axis.
Inherited isolated displacement of the pupil and lens; associated iris and other ocular abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Defined by progressive leukodystrophy and persistent thickened, wrinkled, hyperkeratotic skin; both occur in 80-99%.
Neurodevelopmental disease with hearing loss in 14/14; immunodeficiency in 4/12 (33%). Visual loss is predominantly cerebral; scoliosis 4/14 is below 30%.
CIITA-related combined immunodeficiency; supplied findings do not establish common intrinsic gut, lung or liver damage independent of separately diagnosed infections.
Developmental delay in 8/8; persistent ankyloglossia in 4/7 (57%) and ptosis in 2/5 (40%) support oral and eyelid involvement. Ear shape alone does not establish ear dysfunction.
Malignant fibroblastic tumor predominantly arising in soft connective tissues and bone; organ-specific rare subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Isolated unilateral shortening of finger bones is a structural skeletal malformation.
Toxic degeneration of the retinal macula; the disease itself is ocular regardless of the responsible exposure.
Infantile epilepsy with progressive encephalopathy and cortical atrophy; hypotonia and ataxia reflect neurologic disease.
Intellectual disability, keratoconus and skeletal deformities define the syndrome; hyperlipidemia/obesity occur in 80-99%. Cleft palate and hearing loss (30-79%) omitted by cap.
IRF6 spectrum predominantly causes oral clefting and lower-lip pits; popliteal and other limb abnormalities belong to a minority subtype.
HHV8-associated vascular sarcoma predominantly occupying skin. Pulmonary and gastrointestinal spread are uncommon in the classic form.
Aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma; hematologic neoplasia and the lymphoma mechanism apply. No additional organ is consistently affected above threshold.
Skeletal myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy occur in 5/5; persistent ptosis in 5/5 supports eyelid involvement. Motor delay reflects muscle disease.
Inherited alteration of albumin-mediated thyroid hormone binding causes euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia; it does not establish thyroid injury or hematologic disease.
Muscle fatty replacement/atrophy, inflammatory dermatitis and intestinal lymphangiectasia affect ~50% each. Anemia and developmental delay (~50%) omitted by cap; splenomegaly alone insufficient.
Adenosquamous carcinoma originating in intrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Umbrella defined by congenital multiple joint contractures, sometimes with muscle fibrosis. Neurologic causes vary by subtype and are not universal.
